C-EPOCH-OPEN-DEFAULT-1-CE010A4C.Summary: One `src/` bundle that pays the one staged finding `F308`: an unbounded `ngrace cursor advance --open-epoch` allocates the constant `w0:1-99` on every bundle, so on any bundle with a folded history the next `ngrace cursor fold` refuses `range hole at 1 for w0` and `ngrace cursor recover --fix` declines because the effective covering allocation is `present`. The default lives at `const from = options.from ?? 1;` (`src/grace-cursor.ts:976`, `to = from + 98` at `:977`); the fold's contiguity walk begins at `allocation.from` and reports the first missing id (`src/grace-cursor.ts:2838`–`2843`); `recover --fix` returns `fixApplied: false` whenever the covering allocation is `present` (`src/grace-cursor.ts:678`), and a leading-holed allocation is `present`. `ngrace-execute` rule 12 and the `opened` kind tell every agent to open **without** bounds, so the ordinary instruction produces an unfoldable epoch on every bundle that has already folded once — the finding was met by the executor on this branch's first correction after two folded epochs, and re-measured by the authority on a copy of the same bundle with four folded epochs and an empty `run/`. (The final `--run-commands` writes loose `command-run` events with no allocation — `appendCommandRunEvent`, `src/lint/core.ts:510` — and the fold synthesizes a hole-free covering allocation from the first loose id; it is the *next* `cursor advance --open-epoch` that reaches the `from = 1` default.) The remedy has two parts, both confined to `src/grace-cursor.ts`: the unbounded open derives its `from` from the next event id after the folded history (`nextEventId(bundlePath)`) instead of the constant `1`, so the allocation begins at the `opened` event's own id and the fold's walk begins at a used id; and `recover --fix` treats a present covering allocation whose reported hole lies below every loose event id as a leading hole and re-homes it, while a hole inside the loose range (a genuinely lost event) still declines. The `ngrace-execute` text stands unchanged: the unbounded open becomes correct, and the bounded reopen the finding offered as interim teaching is no longer needed.

Goals.Goal: **`F308` (a) — the unbounded open starts where the events start.** In `advanceCursor` (`src/grace-cursor.ts:972`), the `openEpoch` default becomes `const from = options.from ?? nextEventId(bundlePath);`, never `?? 1`. `nextEventId` already computes `max(floor, looseMax + 1, ledgerMax + 1)`, so it is the id the `opened` event itself receives; the allocation therefore begins at a used id and `allocationsFor(id)` still clamps `from: Math.min(from, id)`. Explicit `--from`/`--to` are unchanged, and `writeEventFile`'s existing renumber-on-collision keeps `allocation.from` at or below the written id. On a fresh bundle `nextEventId` is `1`, so the first unbounded open is byte-identical to today; only a post-fold open moves.

**`F308` (b) — `recover --fix` re-homes a leading hole.** In `recoverCursor` (`src/grace-cursor.ts:678`), `--fix` stops skipping every `present` covering allocation. It skips when the covering is present **and** the fold's reported hole does not lie below every loose event id. When the first reported hole is below the lowest loose id — ids that folded, not lost — `--fix` writes a superseding opened via the shipped `writeCoveringOpened` (append-only, D9; last-writer-wins per worker, D9.1; never a terminal, A29.2 / F12), starting at the first loose id. The post-fix diagnosis reads `Fix applied: yes`, `Fold: ok`, and `Covering opened: run/<id>-<task>-opened.xml`. A hole inside the loose range is a genuinely lost event no verb may fabricate: `--fix` returns `Fix applied: no` and leaves the stream byte-unchanged. Multi-worker still refuses before write (D8.2). No test asserts that a `present` covering is a no-op except where the fold is not holed.

**`F308` (c) — a deterministic red on `main`, and a green after.** Add guards to `src/grace-cursor.test.ts` (no new test file) that red on the base commit and green here, on this platform with no Windows dependency: (i) seed a bundle, open unbounded, progress, terminal, `foldEpoch` applies; open unbounded again, progress, terminal, `foldEpoch` must apply and not throw — on the base commit it throws `invalid-project` naming `range hole at 1 for w0`; (ii) a legacy/ explicit-low leading-holed stream — open explicitly `from: 1`, progress, terminal, fold (green), then open explicitly `from: 1` again, progress, terminal — `recoverCursor({ fix: true })` returns `fixApplied: true` and a following `foldEpoch` applies, where on the base commit it returns `false` and the fold throws; (iii) a mid-range hole — a hand-written allocation with a gap inside the loose range — `recoverCursor({ fix: true })` returns `fixApplied: false` and the fold still throws, in both trees. Keep every existing `AC-UNIQUE-CONCURRENT` / `AC-NO-SILENT-OVERWRITE` / `AC-FORCED-COLLISION` guard green.
